::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 23d [1899]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels/76
:::

My dear [C C](people/person_329.qmd)
If I were to be dissected while I am alive, I think you would do it tenderly, but indeed I have always shrunk from seeing the lives of living people and my whole old fashioned nature revolts at the idea partly personally, and partly because I know how those who are gone would feel about it, so indeed I do not think it is possible to my feelings and I hope you will not be vexed.

We are overwhelmed with applications for the Infant school at Allbrook, having advertised in the [School mistress](organizations/other_212.qmd).  One offers herself from Stirling!  She would be odd here I think.  We have [Mrs Sumner](people/person_1381.qmd)’s presentation next week, all the mothers in the diocese to drink tea at Wolvesey, and the week after our bazaar for the schools- after which from the 3d to the 6th, I go down to the Heathcotes at Beechwood and on the 10th [Annie Moberly](people/person_1024.qmd) comes to me for ten days, and I shall get a dip in Oxford news.  Mr [Cosmo Lang](people/person_2089.qmd) made a splendid speech at the [Higher Religious Education](organizations/other_48.qmd) meeting.

[A D I](people/person_744.qmd)’s promises dont seem to come to anything only he says his company won’t let him get at the money to pay his debts till all is paid in.

I wonder if it would do any good to send a lawyer to call on him or if it would be only sending good money after bad.

He has given no account for my own books, as well as /contributions to\\ the [M P](organizations/other_52.qmd).  If you are not paid for all this past year, I wonder you do not strike but he keeps on pacifying you.

You never mentioned Alice.

your affectionate
C M Yonge
